items.title: [storybook] Storybook: Missing origin validation in Storybook preview allows code injection from malicious websites
items.summary: Summary: A malicious website may be able to cause unauthorized file changes in a developer’s project while an affected Storybook development server is running. Under additional conditions, a changed file could be executed by a local runtime with the developer’s privileges. We are not aware of exploitation in the wild.Who is impacted?You are impacted if you run a Storybook dev server in the affected versions.You are not impacted if:You run a dev server that you never open in a web browser (e.g. headless automation, MCP clients)You run or visit a built version of StorybookRecent versions of Chrome and Firefox may ask for permission before a website can connect to a localhost service. This reduces the risk, but does not remove it. Do not grant this permission to websites you don’t trust.Recommended actionsUpgrade StorybookStorybook has released patched versions of all affected major Storybook versions that fix all the vulnerabilities necessary for the worst-case scenario above to occur. Upgrade to a patched version listed below before running storybook dev again. If you cannot upgrade immediately, do not run an affected Storybook dev server until you can apply the fix.11.0.0-alpha.610.6.29.1.218.6.19Review potentially breaking changesDue to the exceptional nature of the reported vulnerabilities, the Storybook team has decided to change the default behavior of Storybook, including versions 8 and 9, for several network-related features that are not essential to most Storybook users' workflow. If your team relies on the affected features, we've added feature flags that can disable specific security updates to support your existing workflows.Please carefully read the introduced flags and the consequences of using them.Iframe embedding over the network is disabled by defaultStorybook no longer allows the manager or preview to be embedded as an iframe on a website with a different host name. Built versions of Storybook are unaffected and can be freely embedded.If you rely on embedding a Storybook dev server through a separate web app, run that separate app on localhost. You may also use the security.insecureRemoteIframeEmbed feature flag to re-enable iframe embedding from any origin.The preview iframe rejects messages sent by an unknown hostBoth the Storybook preview and manager now restrict the origin of iframes and parent windows that they can send messages to and receive messages from using the postMessage API.By default, Storybook in dev mode only accepts communication with its own origin and other localhost services. Built Storybooks continue to accept communication from unknown origins.A Storybook addon or integration could hypothetically rely on postMessage to update a live story's args. If you do that, reach out to the Storybook team to explore safer alternatives.Storybook composition also relies on postMessage, so a composed Storybook on a different origin now fails to load unless it has been built. The security.insecureIframeMessaging feature flag disables this protection, but we recommend you build composed Storybooks instead.The highlight event signature has changedStorybook’s own accessibility addon uses the highlight event to inject highlights into the preview, which a user can click. Clicking the highlight opens a menu with a link to a documentation page.The API for that event was too permissive and could be used to trigger arbitrary events, including events processed by the user’s dev server. We reworked the API to prevent abuse. Besides the accessibility addon, Chromatic's Visual Tests addon uses this API to link to documentation from highlighted ignored elements. Update the Visual Tests addon to version 5.5.1 or later to keep that link working. Because no other addons use this API as far as we know, we have not added a feature flag to restore the old API.Disclosure timelineOn September 30th, the Storybook team received a responsible disclosure showing how a malicious website can embed a Storybook dev server's preview iframe and send events to the dev server on the developer's machine.They combined this information with findings from an ongoing security audit to come up with a worst-case-scenario exploitation of the disclosed vulnerability, and the ones we independently discovered. They then worked to address all layers necessary for this worst-case scenario to happen. We have not received evidence of exploitation in real Storybook projects. The attack outlined in this advisory relies on correctly exploiting a sequence of many vulnerabilities, some of which were never disclosed to the Storybook team.Worst-case attack scenarioAn attacker-controlled website can interact with the preview of a running Storybook dev server. With user interaction, it may cause the dev server to make unauthorized changes to story files. If a malicious file is subsequently executed by a local runtime, the attack could lead to arbitrary code execution with the developer’s permissions.Referenceshttps://github.com/storybookjs/

items.title: [electron] Electron: HID and USB permission checks can be attributed to the wrong origin
items.summary: ImpactFor hid and usb permission checks made from an iframe, session.setPermissionCheckHandler was given the top-level frame's origin and details instead of the requesting frame's. Apps that allow these permissions based on origin could grant an embedded frame access intended for the top-level page.You're only affected if you use setPermissionCheckHandler with origin-based logic for hid or usb and embed cross-origin iframes with allow="hid" or allow="usb". Apps that don't delegate those features to untrusted iframes are not affected.WorkaroundsDon't add allow="hid" / allow="usb" to untrusted iframes, or make the decision in your select-hid-device / select-usb-device handler using details.frame.Fixed Versions45.0.0-alpha.544.3.043.7.042.11.3For more informationIf you have any questions or comments about this advisory, email us at security@electronjs.orgReferenceshttps://github.com/electron/electron/security/advisories/GHSA-fw47-9c62-h3vwhttps://github.com/electron/electron/pull/53656https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/53679https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/53688https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/53689https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/53736https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/22de0a3a06cfd3174fc6c59c3810ab5e1c91bf1ahttps://github.com/electron/electron/commit/36042b2e1b1c60c67b05ba0e95d1a34f608b9742https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/56cc43eb677d46b86b0d3f49b5fba71404ab1ff0https://github.com/electron/electron/commit/922073f8601479e93071f56f0745041291b206fdhttps://github.com/electron/electron/commit/c965cee73284c4b230a81d51a7db6115e55da8c0https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v42.11.3https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v43.7.0https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v44.3.0https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v45.0.0-alpha.5https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fw47-9c62-h3vw

items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/slugTaken discloses existence of private/admin-only content to any authenticated user
items.summary: SummaryThe slugTaken endpoint returns a boolean indicating whether a slug is in use acrossall document types and visibility levels, with no permission or type filter. Any logged-inuser (including editors) can enumerate the slug space of private pages, drafts, andarchived content.DetailsPOST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/slugTaken with body { "slug": "target-slug" } runsa raw existence check against the documents collection. It does not:Check whether the requesting user has read permission for documents of that type.Filter by visibility (public, loginRequired, private).Filter by viewRole.Filter by publication status (draft vs published).A single authenticated session can iterate the slug space to enumerate the full contentinventory of the CMS, including content the user is explicitly prohibited from viewing.PoC# Any authenticated session works — editor role sufficientcurl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" -X POST \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"slug":"known-private-page-slug"}' \  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/slugTaken"# → { "taken": true }  — confirms private page existscurl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" -X POST \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \  -d '{"slug":"zzz-nonexistent"}' \  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/slugTaken"# → { "taken": false }ImpactInformation disclosure. An attacker with any authenticated session can enumerate allslugs in the system, mapping the full content structure of the CMS including private andadmin-only content.Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-f66c-mpj2-3r8hhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112952https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/06e4b377f3c360f9e89c32dccd7e505ad5ddf498https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/40b989b1a9dd23d30029b8ce7668634265cfe5eahttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/apostrophe@4.34.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f66c-mpj2-3r8h

items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/:id bypasses viewRole restriction and exposes viewPermission-gated fields to lower-privileged users
items.summary: SummaryThe getOne REST endpoint for pages does not apply viewRole type-level restrictionsor viewPermission field-level redaction. An editor-level user who knows a document_id can read the full content of admin-only pages and their privileged fields, whilethe getAll endpoint correctly enforces both restrictions.DetailsFinding 3 — viewRole bypass:modules/@apostrophecms/page/index.js exposes getRestQuery(req, omitPermissionCheck = false). The getAll path calls publicApiCheckAsync and threads the full query builderpipeline including viewRole filtering. The getOne path uses a divergent code paththat skips this pipeline.A page type declared with viewRole: 'admin' is inaccessible via GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page?type=secretPage (returns 403 to an editor) but is fullyreturned by GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/:id:en:published to the same editor.Finding 4 — viewPermission field leak:Fields decorated with viewPermission: { action: 'edit', type: '@apostrophecms/page' }are stripped by removeForbiddenFields in the getAll path but are returned verbatimin getOne. An editor who knows any document _id can read allviewPermission-restricted fields.PoC# Log in as editor, get session jarEDITOR_JAR="..."# getAll — correctly blockedcurl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" \  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page?type=secretPage"# → 403 Forbidden# getOne — bypassed, returns full document including viewPermission fieldscurl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" \  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/ADMIN_PAGE_ID:en:published"# → 200 OK, full doc including secretField valueImpactEditors can read the full content of any page — including those restricted to admins viaviewRole — if they know or can guess the _id. Sensitive field values gated byviewPermission are also fully exposed. This breaks the content access control modelfor any site using these decorators.Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-vh56-5m88-39rqhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112957https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/06e4b377f3c360f9e89c32dccd7e505ad5ddf498https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/40b989b1a9dd23d30029b8ce7668634265cfe5eahttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/apostrophe@4.34.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vh56-5m88-39rq

items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: Stored XSS via Unescaped Widget Style Attribute Serialization
items.summary: SummaryApostropheCMS widget styles support project-defined schema fields. If a project defines a free-form string style field with a CSS property and no selector, an editor-controlled value is rendered as an inline CSS declaration. The resulting declaration is then inserted into the widget wrapper's style="..." attribute without HTML-attribute escaping.An attacker who can edit the widget can include a double quote in the style value, terminate the style attribute, and inject new HTML event-handler attributes. The payload is stored with the widget and executes in the Apostrophe site origin whenever the affected published page is rendered.This is a sibling of CVE-2026-33889 / GHSA-97v6-998m-fp4g. items.title: [@apostrophecms/import-export] ApostropheCMS: Missing Authentication in `cleanExport` Route
items.summary: 1. SummaryThe API endpoint POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/import-export/clean-export in @apostrophecms/import-export lacks authentication and authorization checks. Any client—including unauthenticated anonymous users who have obtained the standard CSRF cookie from visiting the site—can directly invoke this route and trigger the underlying self.cleanExport(req) method.2. Affected Files & EndpointsEndpoint: POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/import-export/clean-exportRoute Definition: packages/import-export/lib/apiRoutes.js (lines 32–34)Method Implementation: packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js (lines 1271–1324)3. Root Cause AnalysisIn packages/import-export/lib/apiRoutes.js, the get.related handler explicitly validates that the caller is logged in:get: {  async related(req) {    if (!req.user) {      throw self.apos.error('forbidden');    }    // ...  }}In contrast, post.cleanExport (as well as post.overrideDuplicates) lacks any verification of req.user:post: {  async overrideDuplicates(req) {    return self.overrideDuplicates(req);  },  async cleanExport(req) {    return self.cleanExport(req); // <-- No authentication check  }}Because ApostropheCMS does not enforce authentication globally on all apiRoutes, omitting an explicit if (!req.user) guard allows anonymous requests to pass directly through to the business logic layer.4. EvidenceWhen sending an unauthenticated POST request with the site’s CSRF cookie (issued to any visitor on GET /), the request bypasses access control entirely and executes self.cleanExport(req), as demonstrated by the server stack trace:at Object.cleanExport (.../packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js)at .../packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/module/index.js:193:30This confirms that execution directly reaches the core import-export handler without an authenticated session.5. ImpactBroken Access Control: Unauthenticated users can invoke cleanup operations and delete temporary export files and artifacts stored on the server.Unauthorized State Mutation: The endpoint allows modifying job records in the database via req.body.jobId (forcing them to ended: true, status: 'completed') and dismissing notifications via req.body.notificationId without verifying whether the resources belong to the requesting caller.6. Suggested Remediation (Patch)Enforce an authentication check in packages/import-export/lib/apiRoutes.js before executing the underlying methods:--- a/packages/import-export/lib/apiRoutes.js+++ b/packages/import-export/lib/apiRoutes.js@@ -26,10 +26,16 @@ module.exports = self => {     get: { ... },     post: {       async overrideDuplicates(req) {+        if (!req.user) {+          throw self.apos.error('forbidden');+        }         return self.overrideDuplicates(req);       },        async cleanExport(req) {+        if (!req.user) {+          throw self.apos.error('forbidden');+        }         return self.cleanExport(req);       }     }Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-rw26-wwfc-9wvmhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-113648https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/06e4b377f3c360f9e89c32dccd7e505ad5ddf498https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/40b989b1a9dd23d30029b8ce7668634265cfe5eahttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/@apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rw26-wwfc-9wvm
